resolved_suspects.description: Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar6` self-updates via pointer arithmetic on its own `filename` field (which decays to a pointer), `+ CONST`; `offsetof(filename) + CONST*sizeof(elem)` equals the stride of a *different* array the loop reads through `pCVar6`. Replace those `pCVar6->other_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update. (String/buffer-copy cursors that only touch the advanced field are excluded here — those are unrolled_strcpy/unrolled_memcpy.)

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `this_ptr` self-updates via pointer arithmetic on its own `filename` field (which decays to a pointer), `+ CONST`; `offsetof(filename) + CONST*sizeof(elem)` equals the stride of a *different* array the loop reads through `this_ptr`. Replace those `this_ptr->other_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update. (String/buffer-copy cursors that only touch the advanced field are excluded here — those are unrolled_strcpy/unrolled_memcpy.)

Ghidra pre-increment-array-walk loop artifact on `piVar3` (struct-field or pointer-arithmetic advance + constant index + self-assign no-op). Always wrong as-decoded; cross-reference .asm and rewrite as a straightforward for-loop in a .keep (watch for the skip-row store-offset bug).
resolved_suspects.match: do { var = var(+N|->...); var[K]/arr[0]...; var = var; ...}
